errors.text: The proposed screw-dislocation kink-pair mechanism is imported from a BCC MoNbTaW refractory HEA and is not established for FCC FeNiCrMn.

The target mechanism is nucleation of Shockley partial dislocations at vacancy clusters or disordered sites, followed by stacking-fault formation; the hypothesis instead assigns yielding to pre-existing screw-dislocation glide.
The loading-rate range is reconstructed incorrectly as 10^-4–10^3 s^-1 rather than the molecular-dynamics range of 10^8–10^10 s^-1.
The required orientation anisotropy is not recovered: the specific <110>, <1-12>, and <-111> loading directions and maximum yield stress along <-111> are omitted.
The hypothesis does not account for the observed increase in dislocation density and flow stress with strain rate through kinetically limited dislocation annihilation.
Relevant evidence for partial-dislocation behavior in an FCC HEA is cited but does not support the asserted screw-dislocation kink-pair mechanism.
